title: The Real Cost of "Just Paying the Minimum"
description:
A $5,000 credit card balance at 24% APR, paid off with minimum payments only. We work out exactly how many years that takes, how much of it is pure interest, and what changes when you pay a fixed amount instead of the shrinking minimum.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#creditcarddebt #debtpayoff #personalfinance

segments.text: A five thousand dollar credit card balance. Minimum payments only. Here's how long that actually takes to pay off.
Minimum payments are usually a small percentage of your balance, often around three percent, or a flat amount, whichever is higher.
At a typical twenty-four percent interest rate, most of that minimum payment is just covering the interest, not the debt itself.
The balance creeps down so slowly it barely looks like progress for years at a time.
Sixteen years and nine months. That's how long it takes to clear that balance on minimums alone.
And the interest paid along the way? Eight thousand four hundred forty-one dollars. More than the original balance itself.
Pay a fixed amount instead of the shrinking minimum, and the picture changes completely.

slide.headline: Total interest paid, by payment strategy

segments.text: The minimum payment isn't designed to get you out of debt fast. It's designed to keep the balance alive.

lines: Every extra dollar compounds in your favor.
